# WHAT IT IS FOR. gates.sh builds its gate list by globbing gates/regress/*.js, so it counts the gates it FINDS.
# A gate that was deleted, renamed, or never merged is therefore indistinguishable from a gate that was never
# needed, and the suite still ends "GATES GREEN". Measured at #450 and again here: gates/regress/67-sel-cls-
# consumers.js, the only gate that reddens on the sel/cls consumer P0s, is absent from main, and
# gates/regress/50-drill-verdict-no-jump.js was authored 2026-09-22 for the drill board jump and committed by
# nobody. Main's suite reported 47 suites green with both of them missing and no tool in this project said so.
# HOW IT IS READ. gates/gatemanifest.sh check compares this file against gates/regress/ on disk:
#   state=required  MUST be on disk. Absent  -> gates.sh FAILS BEFORE RUNNING ANY GATE and cannot emit GATES GREEN.
#   state=absent    known to exist somewhere and NOT on main. Reported loudly on every run; does NOT redden.
#   state=retired   deliberately removed. The row STAYS - see "a row is never deleted" below. Does not redden.
#   no row at all   UNLISTED: the suite still runs (a new gate must be able to), but the footer records it and
#                   gates/verify-log.sh REFUSES the log, so a gate cannot reach main without a row here.
# A ROW IS NEVER DELETED, which is the whole mechanism and is borrowed from gates/build-numbers.tsv. To remove a
# gate you run `gates/gatemanifest.sh retire <gate> '<why>'`, which flips state to retired and writes the reason
# INTO THIS FILE, so the removal appears in a commit diff with its justification attached. Deleting the row
# instead would make the manifest agree with the deletion silently, which is the defect this file exists to stop.
# WHY required IS NOT "EVERY GATE THAT HAS EVER EXISTED" [CLAUDE.md, #405, the frozen denominator]. The 47
# required rows below are seeded from the committed suite at #461 and nothing else. THEIR PROVENANCE, STATED
# HONESTLY RATHER THAN INVENTED: the build and date columns read 461 / 2026-10-02 for all 47 because that is when
# the ROW was written, NOT when the gate was introduced - those build numbers are recoverable from git log and are
# deliberately not guessed here. The `covers` column is each gate's own header comment, truncated, not a fresh
# fields: gate <TAB> state <TAB> build <TAB> at <TAB> who <TAB> covers <TAB> note

Drives SIX NAMED lessons because the CTA's y is per-lesson, plus Openings row 20 for block F. EXTENDED AT #498 (the 100vh cap and the panel scroller; B1b moved from a fullyOnScreen ceiling of 2 to REACHABILITY at a ceiling of ZERO, because 2<=2 held on the broken AND the fixed bundle; block D added) AND AGAIN AT #505. #505's OWN CHANGES, every one of them forced by an upheld blind-antagonist veto rather than chosen: (1) B1b's and block C's reachability filters now read computed `touch-action` down the whole ancestor chain, not just overflow-y and room - they answered a question about what SCRIPT can scroll while every message built on them said 'what a FINGER can scroll', and on a control bundle with touch-action:'none' on the panel and both inner blocks, where six real finger drags move nothing and a player can never reach the card's own button, the gate scored 78 pass / 2 fail with B1b, B1d, B1bG, B1bG2, C0 and C1 ALL GREEN. BOTH copies of the walk had to be fixed: correcting only userScrollables left C0 passing from block C's uncorrected copy in the same run. (2) D1 IS NOW A NOTE AND NOT A VERDICT. #498 committed it as a hard assertion ('Both must hold') that one drag brings the CTA into the viewport, and it reads IDENTICALLY on the fixed and control bundles at both geometries, to the digit - capture changes which element HEARS a scroll, not which element SCROLLS - so it has zero discriminating power for this fix and at short375 it is a positive control credited as a PASS. Its property is stricter than US-R50's own words and is the deliverable of jobs/the-intro-cards-primary-button-should-not-be-below-its-own-fold-2026-10-08. The measurement is still printed every run. (3) D1b replaces it as D2's denominator (a child of the panel actually scrolled), and D2G is the hard global anti-vacuity guard for block D. (4) BLOCK F IS NEW AND IT ASSERTS THE OTHER SIDE OF THE HOLD: on a card whose panel has NO scroll room and whose button is already on screen, a descendant scroll with no click must NOT pin the card. #505's own first fix held it indefinitely there - measured card-up at +4600, +12000 and +20000ms on Openings row 20 at 320x568, over a demo that had autoplayed to its end - and the population is 80 of 97 Openings rows at that geometry, which no assertion in this suite reached. F0d and F0e are its preconditions and F1G is the global guard that the population exists in the run. F scrolls programmatically and SAYS SO rather than claiming a finger it did not use. (5) D3a is a NOTE printing what pinning overflow-x costs (0 hidden px at all three geometries driven, 35 at 256 wide, 74 at 213), and the claim that `hidden` DELETES the Related chip is WITHDRAWN - both antagonists measured it false independently: 183.39 of 216.89px remain painted at 256 wide, 84.6%, with the centre tappable and a real tap opening the Related lesson.
